prose: A long reflection, 'What I saw around the Curve, 2026', that cites the argument that even incremental AI capability gains, with no coordinated power-seeking, risk eventual human disempowerment because machine alternatives become more competitive across labor, decisions, art and companionship. It mixes that with reported political anecdotes from the policy world. Basis: excerpts from the start of a long piece.
highlights: Argues gradual capability gains can disempower humans without any sudden takeover.
Competitive machine alternatives in labor, decision-making, art and companionship drive it.
Includes anecdotes from the policy scene.
